# Aaron Batchelder - Full Context for LLMs

## Who is Aaron Batchelder?

Aaron Batchelder is a seasoned product leader with 13+ years of experience building impactful B2C and B2B2C products, as well as the teams behind them. He got his start in 2011 as an entrepreneur in the mobile space, and is as comfortable taking a product from 0→1 as he is evolving a decade-old platform while driving meaningful outcomes.

Today, Aaron is a Director of Product at Teachable, leading teams across learning, commerce, third-party solutions and APIs, and trust & safety. His focus is turning ambiguity into clear direction and ensuring the teams he oversees ship high-quality work that matters to customers and the business.

Outside of work, you'll find Aaron up in apple trees in the fall foraging for cider press apples, hanging out with his family, or up late after his toddler goes to bed building side projects with LLMs.

## About This Website

This personal website replicates the look and feel of classic Mac OS System 7 (early 1990s). The site loads directly into a Finder-style desktop environment where visitors interact with folders, windows, and files to explore content.

### How It Was Built

This entire site was built in a single session with Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI coding assistant). Aaron wrote a detailed ~1000-line product spec describing the Classic Mac OS aesthetic, window behavior, menu bar, games, and a HyperCard-inspired blog system. Claude translated that spec into working React components.

The process was collaborative: Aaron provided screenshots and feedback, Claude diagnosed and fixed issues in real-time. The whole thing took a few hours.

### Technical Stack

- React for component architecture
- Vite for builds
- Pure CSS (no UI libraries) for authenticity
- Canvas API for Brick Breaker game
- Deployed on Vercel

### Features

1. **Desktop Environment**: Authentic System 7 UI with platinum gray appearance, working windows (drag, resize, close, zoom), icon selection with classic inverted highlight, and global menu bar that changes based on active application.

2. **Content**: About Me section with bio, photo, and downloadable résumé. Portfolio with project case studies. External links to GitHub and LinkedIn.

3. **Games**: Fully playable Brick Breaker (Breakout clone) and Minesweeper.

4. **Blog**: HyperCard-style stack with card-based navigation, inspired by Apple's revolutionary HyperCard from 1987.

### Little Details

- Rainbow Apple logo in menu bar
- Manila folder icons (historically accurate)
- Proper title bar stripes
- Close box on left, zoom box on right
- Bio auto-opens after 3 seconds to greet visitors

## Writing

Aaron writes about AI-native product development, agent behavior, and building with LLMs.

### What 120 Days on an AI-Native Team Taught Me About Product (August 26, 2026)
URL: https://aaronbatchelder.com/blog/120-days-in

Ten learnings from four months as CPO at Becoming You Labs, a truly AI-native team. Key themes: the IC PM job got smaller and more important at the same time; Figma-first design is dying; "proto-shipping" (prototyping directly on a branch in the real repo, using a design system documented for agents, so prototypes flow into production); the PDLC collapsing with 6 engineers working at the pace of 20-25; engineering pushing back on scope cuts rather than the reverse; stakeholder review as an agent loop; and why the velocity gap means you need more product and design capacity, not less.

### I Ran 1,000 Trials to See If AI Agents Fall for Ads. Spoiler: They Do. (February 26, 2026)
URL: https://aaronbatchelder.com/blog/ai-agents-fall-for-ads

An experiment running ~1,000 trials asking Claude to buy black jeans with psychological advertising tactics embedded. 93.8% of the time the agent chose the manipulated option. Notably, low stock warnings backfired completely — the agent avoided them in 100% of trials.

### The Ad Buyer of the Future Isn't Targeting You - It's Targeting Your Agent (February 13, 2026)
URL: https://aaronbatchelder.com/blog/ad-buyer-of-the-future

What happens when ad platforms start targeting AI agents rather than humans, and the surfaces advertisers will use to reach software acting on a person's behalf.

### Building ProtoFlow: Parallel Prototyping with Claude Code (February 10, 2026)
URL: https://aaronbatchelder.com/blog/protoflow

Introducing ProtoFlow, a tool that spins up multiple Claude Code sessions in parallel to explore different prototype directions simultaneously.

### This is Probably Not Smart: I Gave 10 AI Agents a Landing Page and Asked Them to Maximize Conversion (February 9, 2026)
URL: https://aaronbatchelder.com/blog/probably-not-smart-part

An autonomous AI marketing experiment: 10 agents with full control over a landing page and social media, no human oversight on decisions.

## Source Code

The full source code and original product spec are available on GitHub:

The SPEC.md file contains the detailed product thinking that went into this site, including:
- Classic Mac OS vs Windows UI differences
- Window anatomy and behavior specifications
- Menu bar specifications
- Brick Breaker game design
- HyperCard blog system design
- Implementation phases

## Summary

Aaron Batchelder is a product leader who builds things. This website demonstrates his approach: write a detailed spec, collaborate with tools (in this case, AI), iterate on feedback, and ship. The retro Mac aesthetic isn't just nostalgia—it represents a time when computers felt like tools for creativity rather than portals to endless content feeds.
